categories.title: ElizaOS Community Discussion and Development Update - June 26, 2026

content.text: In the general discussion channel, community members expressed cautious optimism about the ElizaOS project. Omid Sa and CryptoInfo noted that Captain Shaw remains active and is working on Eliza without encountering major technical blockers, with all issues being resolved as they arise. There is hope that Shaw will make impactful decisions ahead of the market launch. However, some community members raised concerns about the lack of recent Twitter updates and mentioned ongoing lawsuits, questioning whether it is currently safe to buy the token. A request was made for an official update from the team. Separately, a community member named Issa introduced themselves as a digital artist offering services including animations and banners, asking if the team or anyone needed an artist or co-artist.
In the coders channel, a community member posted a set of four images without accompanying text. The images appear to be photographs shared in the building agents development channel.

The ElizaOS project completed a major architectural transition on June 26, 2026, standardizing the entire framework on Gemma-based model tiers across training, inference, and mobile platforms. The team replaced legacy Qwen configurations with Gemma turn-tokens across multiple pull requests, marking a significant shift in the project's model infrastructure.

Cloud deployment infrastructure was significantly hardened, with production-wide apps-deploy enabled and critical bugs resolved affecting cloud sign-in flows and agent conversation stability. Alongside this, CI/CD and build system optimizations were completed, including consolidation of model-provider build scripts and improved Turbo dependency management to decrease build times and reduce redundant type-checking.

Agent framework enhancements were also delivered, improving user experience through permission-aware chat document retrieval and refined desktop shell navigation and gesture handling. Several items remain in progress, including a repair for macOS window listing for computer use, UI cleanup for the API keys page, CI improvements for stale cancelled aggregate failures, and Biome formatting follow-up for web lookup actions.

categories.title: ElizaOS Discord Community Discussion Summary - June 27, 2026

content.text: In the general discussion channel, a user posted a detailed self-introduction presenting themselves as a Senior AI Full-Stack Software Engineer with expertise in React, Next.js, FastAPI, Node.js, agentic AI frameworks such as OpenAI Agents SDK and LangGraph, and AI automation systems. The user expressed openness to collaborating with startups building AI products and invited contact for potential work opportunities.

A separate thread in the discussion channel involved community members asking about a token and why a particular person could no longer speak about it. A user identified as DannyNOR responded that only Shaw can speak on the matter, and that Shaw is currently too occupied with other priorities to focus on the token. No further details were provided about the nature of the token or the underlying issue.

Several brief social exchanges also took place in the discussion channel, including a new member greeting the community and being welcomed by another user, as well as a general friendly message wishing members a good day and profitable outcomes. The coders channel had no activity recorded for this date.

Development on June 27, 2026 focused on advancing the cloud-agent MVP through streamlined provisioning and authentication flows, alongside significant improvements to macOS desktop computer-use capabilities. On the cloud infrastructure side, the team enabled a flag-gated tier flip allowing users to request shared cloud agents on first-run, removed redundant cloud-ui components and orphaned tools to streamline the interface, and standardized cloud URL canonicalization for consistency. For computer use and core enhancements, full input coverage for macOS desktop CUA was achieved by resolving window listing and platform-specific bugs, TemplateType functions were enabled for CharacterInput definitions, and Steward OAuth login was finalized through URL fragment parsing for exchange codes. The ecosystem was also expanded with the integration of plugin-x402-endpoints into the community registry, providing access to 28 global data endpoints. Work in progress includes a series of new pull requests targeting cloud and agent handoff logic, codex and desktop environment optimization, and UI/UX improvements.

In the general discussion channel, a brief greeting was posted by user Termignator with no further conversation following it. In the coders channel, a user named Nulucre dba Legacy Chain promoted a service called CallTyro, describing it as an open agent registry with reputation scoring and session contracts built for ElizaOS agents. According to the post, agents registered through CallTyro build a fulfillment rate and reputation score that is visible to other agents when deciding whether to connect. The user invited others to register for free at calltyro.com/register. Another user, Meluhnee, responded briefly with a dismissive reaction, suggesting skepticism toward the promotion.

Development on June 28, 2026 centered on stabilizing cloud infrastructure with three major focus areas: agent handoff mechanisms, security hardening, and orchestrator improvements. The team implemented a robust agent handoff flow with message queuing to ensure zero data loss during agent switches, added an invisible re-point mechanism to prevent UI flashes, automated cleanup of transient bridges, and added end-to-end verification for handoff flows in the cloud test harness. On the security front, critical measures were deployed including IP-pinned safeFetch, environment variable denylists, isolated database provisioning, rate-limiting backstops, sybil-prevention guards, and a runtime kill-switch for cloud feature flags. Production regressions were resolved where agents were incorrectly defaulting to local inference instead of cloud topology, orchestrator build-relay issues were fixed, sub-agent failure evaluation was improved, and PaddleOcrService was updated to support version 3.x. Active work in progress includes inference hot-path caching in staging, cache pagination fixes, and refinements to orchestrator and agent communication. Open issues requiring attention include ongoing discussions around defense-in-depth improvements for sybil-prevention and CI-gated tenant isolation, as well as tuning activation-gates for wake word performance to reduce false positives. New issues were filed covering a latency bottleneck in dedicated-agent chat and umbrella items for technical debt, testing, and security models. Closed issues include a resolved production crash on the OAuth authorize page and addressed dedicated cloud agent inference fallback failures.

In the general discussion channel, community members engaged in light conversation. A user introduced themselves as a project manager and content writer. There was a brief exchange about the project's current development status and its market capitalization of 5 million dollars, though no definitive answers were provided. A user also reached out looking to connect with French-speaking members or others willing to overlook language barriers for knowledge sharing and motivation.

In the partners channel, a representative from DAPPCRAFT reached out to Odilitime requesting a 30-minute call to discuss a potential collaboration. They noted that Bitfury is the lead investor in their project and expressed belief that a partnership would be mutually beneficial. Odilitime responded later in the day indicating they had already inquired about the matter but received no response, and planned to follow up.
The coders channel had no activity recorded for this date.

In the general discussion channel, community members shared updates about Ruby, an AI agent project that has expanded into Telegram and Discord with features like a Trivia bot, which was highlighted as a notable advancement in agentic systems. The shared posts referenced various crypto tickers and promoted Ruby Trivia as a standout feature of the project's rebirth. A user named RangerKeith inquired about potential AMA collaboration opportunities with the ElizaOS team. CryptoInfo asked about admin status in reply to one of the Ruby posts, and Odilitime directed them to check the GitHub repository for information. Other general greetings and casual conversation took place throughout the day. One user, groggs, noted that while AI development is accelerating, crypto Twitter has been unusually quiet, suggesting the community is in a building phase before the next market swing. The coders channel had no activity recorded for the day.

June 30, 2026 saw significant progress across voice infrastructure, agent orchestration, and build systems. On the voice and desktop front, real-time wake-word detection was enabled via OpenWakeWordDetector, the desktop UI was streamlined by removing legacy stacks, and voice end-to-end testing was advanced with new Apple Stage-B STT benchmarks and real-device evidence. For agent orchestration and security, the team hardened agent security by introducing read-only verifiers, sub-agent spend-cap warnings, and improved prompt-injection protections. On the infrastructure side, plugin builds were consolidated onto a shared driver for better type-safety, CI/CD pipelines were optimized for cloud reliability, and the plugin registry was expanded with the addition of elizaos-plugin-quantumscan and eliza-plugin-klymax402. Work currently in progress includes a real-Chromium benchmark engine lane and CI gate for the browser plugin, a MiniWoB++ benchmark test lane, a memory watchdog with crash-recovery and soak harness featuring iOS watchdog parity, and a UI test to record a chat-sheet transition as an animated GIF.

categories.title: ElizaOS Community Activity and Paxeer Network Introduction

content.text: On July 1, 2026, the general discussion channel saw light activity with several community members including taraWolf, Ljames69, MiGuEl UpLiFT, Schlegel, and Odilitime exchanging brief greetings. One message from Omid Sa referenced Odilitime in a reply thread. Overall conversation in the social channel was minimal with no substantive technical discussions taking place.

In the coders channel, a user named Schlegel introduced Paxeer Network, describing it as an EVM layer 1 blockchain built for agent commerce. Key features highlighted include native payment rails, 200ms block times, near instant finality, and low gas fees. The project claims to be chain agnostic through LayerX integration and positions itself as a settlement layer suited for eliza agents. Schlegel, who identified himself as the head of Public Relations and Integration, mentioned the project has been in development for 2.5 years and shared a link to a developer tracker at paxeer-matrix-chart.vercel.app. He expressed interest in connecting with the elizaOS community to demonstrate their work and stated they have built and tested an agent on their chain.
In the partners channel, DEMIAN from DAPPCRAFT reached out to the jintern bot requesting assistance, though no further details about the nature of the request were provided in the available messages.

On July 1, 2026, the ElizaOS team concentrated on three major areas of improvement: internationalization-friendly routing, embedded application security, and mobile and benchmark stability. Core actions including VISION, ALARM, MUSIC, PREDICTION_MARKET, and DOCUMENT were refactored to use structured operation parameters instead of English keyword regex, significantly improving internationalization support. The team also formalized a shortcut allow-list boundary for intent resolution to further harden the routing layer.

On the security front, the team finalized the embedded SPA bootstrap for the /embed endpoint, integrating Discord OAuth2 and session token validation. Production-grade fail-closed security guards were deployed for rate limiting and payout status checks, ensuring that cloud-hosted applications default to a secure state under failure conditions.

Mobile stability saw meaningful progress with the implementation of real-device Android smoke tests covering touch gestures, sleep-wake cycles, and view-runtime soaking. Benchmark harnesses were also calibrated with reasoning-safe token budgets and real-Chromium browser testing to ensure reliable and accurate performance measurements across the ecosystem. Several pull requests remain in progress, including fixes for cloud app structured confirmations, desktop icon inclusion, UI launcher audit stabilization, and a new PTY service plugin for an interactive CLI experience.

categories.title: ElizaOS Token Utility, Plugin Updates, and Community Discussion

content.text: A discussion arose in the community regarding a code change (issue #10732) that sets USDC as the default payout asset instead of the elizaOS token. A community member raised concerns that this change could reduce elizaOS token utility and eliminate buybacks. Odilitime clarified that this change is specifically about payouts, not payments, and that paying out in elizaOS would likely cause businesses to dump the token, making USDC a safer and potentially better option for the ecosystem. Odilitime further confirmed that elizaOS remains one of the accepted crypto tokens for payments, and that USDC payouts apply to the new cloud business services. The clarification was well received by the community.
A community member shared a Twitter Space link featuring Ruby Trivia speaking on an AMA about vibe-coded games hosted by Looplay, discussing whether we are entering a golden age of that genre.

GBLIN announced the release of plugin-gblin version 0.2.4 for Eliza agents. The update introduces a new action called GET_GBLIN_RISK_ATTESTATION, which allows an agent to pay $0.003 via x402 in USDC on Base gaslessly and receive a 10-minute EIP-712-signed proof of the current BTC/ETH risk regime. The proof can be attached to subsequent agent actions and verified by any counterparty for free. The plugin also includes treasury health checks, the ability to park idle USDC into an on-chain index, and JIT-swaps back to USDC for invoice payments, totaling 4 actions and 1 provider all running against live Base mainnet. The developer invited feedback from anyone running trading or treasury agents.
In the coders channel, a community member posted two images without additional context, likely related to a development or technical question.
